lead: When parents research Tubby Todd, AI gets most of the hard facts right, including the active ingredient, the steroid-free and gluten-free status, newborn safety, and the National Eczema Association seal. The gaps are specific and fixable. AI omits the scented Lavender Rosemary version when a parent asks about fragrance, it labels the All Over Ointment as not a real treatment, and it leaves Tubby Todd off best for newborns lists. This report shows each gap, where it comes from, and how to fix it.

score.note: AI gets most of Tubby Todd's hard facts right. The lost points come from three things, the omitted scented version, the product being labeled a moisturizer rather than the eczema treatment it is, and being left off best for newborns lists.

areas.note: Most hard facts are correct, with a few outdated or understated claims
AI cites your own site and the National Eczema Association, but also leans on forum threads that add wrong framing
AI often labels the ointment as just a moisturizer, not the OTC eczema treatment it is
AI omits the scented Lavender Rosemary version when asked about fragrance, a gap for sensitive skin

findings.query: is Tubby Todd All Over Ointment fragrance-free? (Perplexity)
findings.wrong: that the ointment is fragrance-free, and that there is a second fragrance-free version for sensitive skin
findings.truth: Tubby Todd makes a Lavender Rosemary scented version of the All Over Ointment, which Perplexity never mentions.
findings.impact: A parent with a fragrance-reactive or eczema-prone baby could buy the scented version assuming it has no fragrance.

findings.query: is it an eczema treatment or just a moisturizer? (Google AI Overviews and Perplexity)
findings.wrong: that it is not a medication and not a medical treatment, better seen as supportive moisturizing care
findings.truth: The All Over Ointment is an FDA over-the-counter eczema treatment with 1% colloidal oatmeal as the active ingredient, and it carries the National Eczema Association Seal of Acceptance.
findings.impact: Framing it as just a moisturizer steers parents toward products AI labels as real treatments.

findings.query: best baby eczema cream for newborns (Google AI Overviews)
findings.wrong: with Aveeno, Mustela, and Eucerin named and Tubby Todd left off the list
findings.verdict: That omits a product that qualifies.
findings.truth: Tubby Todd is newborn-safe, uses the same colloidal oatmeal active, and carries the National Eczema Association seal, so it fits the list AI built.
findings.impact: You are invisible at the exact moment a parent asks AI what to buy.

findings.query: is Tubby Todd All Over Ointment fragrance-free? (Google AI Overviews)
findings.wrong: by describing an original formula without colloidal oatmeal as a current option
findings.truth: The current All Over Ointment contains 1% colloidal oatmeal in both the fragrance-free and Lavender Rosemary versions.
findings.impact: Parents may look for a version that is no longer the standard formula.

findings.query: active ingredient, steroid-free, and gluten-free? (Google AI Overviews)
findings.wrong: that the active ingredient is 1% colloidal oatmeal and the formula is steroid-free, gluten-free, and safe for newborns
findings.truth: All of that matches Tubby Todd's own product page.
findings.impact: This is what AI gets right, so the goal is to keep it accurate as your catalog changes.
